topics: APAC edge activation timeline and burst capacity
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Amir (CSM) — Ravi (CTO), Sophie (Head of Platform), Aisha (Procurement), Ethan (SRE)
Links shared: pricing spreadsheet (drive.redwood/pricing-celestia), benchmark template (sheets.red/pricing-bench), SOC2 packet (redwood.share/soc2-2025)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, quick agenda — align on renewal approach, talk APAC edge activation, and agree on next steps.
[00:18] Ravi: cool, thanks Maya. We wanted to make sure we can get APAC online without blowing the budget and also lock in a short extension so we don't lapse while procurement runs.
[00:32] Sophie: yes we have spike traffic in singapore for a pilot next month, need predictable latency under 150ms p95 for tokenization path.
[00:45] Jordan: great — small clarifier, when you say tokenization path is that the full card flow with 3kB payloads? or a lighter path?
[00:58] Sophie: full flow, basically same payloads we used in the sandbox tests, around 2.5–3kB per request.
[01:08] Ethan: and we care about both latency and throughput — our ingest peaks at about 600 rps during promos.
[01:18] Maya: noted. To frame options, we sketched three approaches: keep Hosted with APAC region only (fastest GTM), reserve Dedicated capacity with APAC nodes (predictable throughput), or a hybrid with Dedicated core and hosted burst.
[01:38] Ravi: what's the delta on cost between hosted burst vs dedicated? we need ballpark.
[01:45] Maya: I posted a preliminary sheet — but rough numbers: hosted at current usage scales linearly, Dedicated has a fixed monthly commit but lower per-token cost and predictable SLOs. For APAC burst we can add a small node pool that only bills when used — that helps with cost spikes.
[02:05] Aisha: procurement question — how flexible is the contract term? we prefer quarterly right now given uncertain forecasts.
[02:15] Maya: we can do a 30-day extension to bridge the procurement window and then commit to a 12-month for Dedicated once benchmarks look good. That's what we've recommended for similar finserv customers.
[02:28] Sophie: can you confirm data residency for APAC? we need logs and tokens to stay in region — and KMS must be customer-managed.
[02:38] Amir: yes, for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering, audit logs can be retained in-region. For Hosted we have region-scoped tenancy but KMS must be integrated — we'll send the KMS guide.
[02:55] Ethan: any compliance gaps? SOC2 and ISO?
[03:00] Amir: Redwood's SOC2 Type II report and ISO cert are available — I'll attach them after the call. There are small caveats for on-prem but generally supported.
[03:12] Jordan: on the performance side — to hit 150ms p95 we recommend kernel opt, quantization profile, and continuous batching tuned to the token distribution. Also, KV cache config matters for chat-like flows, though for card-tokenization it's less relevant.
[03:31] Ravi: KV what?
[03:33] Jordan: KV cache, like the key-value cache for long-context models — sorry, that was a bad shorthand. Not critical for the tokenization path.
[03:40] Sophie: got it. For timelines: we want APAC active by June 15 for a pilot. Is that feasible?
[03:47] Maya: if we get the extension signed and we provision a small Dedicated pool or APAC burst, yes. Provisioning Dedicated nodes takes about 7–10 business days after signature. Hosted region can be enabled in 48 hours.
[04:00] Ravi: so short-term move is to enable hosted APAC region and run benchmark; longer-term move to Dedicated if throughput/latency are stable.
[04:09] Maya: exactly. Jordan — can you run a 72-hour throughput run against the APAC endpoint?
[04:15] Jordan: yes, we'll need sample payloads and a runbook; Sophie can share the traffic profile. We'll use the benchmark template.
[04:24] Sophie: i'll drop the payloads in the shared sheet after the call.
[04:28] Aisha: on pricing — if we do a Dedicated commit what's the discount tier for 12 months?
[04:33] Maya: depends on token commit; for the tiers you're looking at (roughly 300k tokens/day) we can offer a mid-tier discount plus an APAC burst credit. I'll share concrete numbers.
[04:44] Ethan: any fallbacks if APAC node latency spikes?
[04:47] Jordan: yes routing policy — we can failover to existin' EU node or degrade to a cheaper quantized model with slightly higher latency but preserve availability. We'll set automatic fallback rules.
[05:00] Ravi: speaking of models, are you using open models or vendor models? we have strict IP concerns.
[05:06] Maya: we host a curated catalog of open weights and Redwood-verified binaries; for Dedicated you can pin specific model versions. We don't use third-party vendor models without customer opt-in.
[05:18] Sophie: good. For procurement, Aisha asked if you accept standard PO and net-30?
[05:24] Aisha: correct.
[05:26] Maya: yes we accept PO and net-30 for Enterprise deals; I'll flag legal for contract addendum for the short extension.
[05:33] Aisha: any SLA credits if uptime dips during pilot?
[05:36] Maya: SLA credits apply on Dedicated annual commits; for a short extension we can include a limited SLA addendum with pro-rated credits — Jordan/Amir we'll need to scope that.
[05:45] Amir: noted — we'll draft language.
[05:48] Jordan: about the benchmark — target metrics we'll measure: p95 latency under 150ms, p99 under 400ms, and error rate <0.5% across 72 hours. Also CPU/GPU utilization target so we can size the Dedicated pool.
[06:03] Ethan: those p99 numbers look high but ok as an initial target.
[06:07] Ravi: can we get a sim of cost per 100k tokens at both hosted and Dedicated?
[06:14] Maya: yes — I'll include that in the pricing spreadsheet.
[06:17] Sophie: what about KMS integration: we use AWS KMS with an external key — can Redwood integrate?
[06:23] Amir: we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys in Dedicated; Hosted supports bring-your-own-key via a limited integration. I'll include the exact steps and the HSM considerations.
[06:36] Sophie: perfect.
[06:38] Jordan: quick note — if you choose Dedicated for APAC we recommend a small GPU profile with latency-optimized kernels; we can test with quantized 4-bit profile to reduce cost while keeping latency acceptable.
[06:49] Ravi: i'm worried about model regressions with quantization. How do you detect quality regressions?
[06:54] Jordan: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring tied to prompt sets — we can run baseline evals on your tokenization outputs and alert on regressions. We also keep reroll capabilities to fallback to a full precision variant.
[07:08] Sophie: that's helpful.
[07:11] Aisha: timeline recap?
[07:13] Maya: Aisha, procurement aims to sign extension this week — if you can confirm by Thursday we'll enable hosted APAC and Jordan will run the 72-hour. Amir sends SOC2/KMS docs by Friday. Follow-up meeting scheduled for 2026-06-02 at 10am PT.
[07:31] Ethan: ok sounds good.
[07:33] Ravi: one more Q on billing — can we show usage by route so we can attribute token spend to transactions?
[07:39] Amir: yes the Console has per-route granularity and token-level dashboards; we'll share screenshots.
[07:46] Maya: any competitors in the mix? Ravi earlier mentioned LambdaCloud, any other?
[07:51] Ravi: AltServe is also in procurement, they had lower latency in our bench last month but less mature security integrations.
[07:59] Jordan: then we'll make sure to highlight KMS/HSM and audit log retention in the comparison.
[08:05] Sophie: OK thanks everyone.

[08:10] Close / recap: 30-day extension to bridge procurement; enable hosted APAC quickly; run 72-hour benchmark; share pricing and security artifacts; follow-up 2026-06-02 10am PT.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 2/Engineer) and typos — speakers sometimes overlap.

End of transcript.
